Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $I_1,\ldots,I_r$ be pairwise comaximal ideals, where $r\ge1$. Then the canonical map
$$ R\longrightarrow \prod_{i=1}^r R/I_i,\qquad x\longmapsto(x+I_1,\ldots,x+I_r) $$
is surjective, its kernel is $\bigcap_{i=1}^r I_i$, and
$$ \bigcap_{i=1}^r I_i=\prod_{i=1}^r I_i. $$
Equivalently,
$$ R/\prod_{i=1}^r I_i\cong\prod_{i=1}^r R/I_i. $$

derivations.claim: **Per-position polynomial projectors and integer spectra.** At rank zero, $H_0(m)=\mathbb C$ has no polynomial generators, the sole empty-word projector and content projector are $1$, and the sector is the single ground-field block with its usual vector duality. Thus all rank-zero assertions follow directly; the spectral argument below concerns $d\ge1$. The finite-dimensional algebra has a faithful regular representation. For adjacent dots put $\delta=x_r-x_{r+1}$ and $\phi_r=s_r\delta+1$. The native cross relations give $\phi_rx_r=x_{r+1}\phi_r$, $\phi_rx_{r+1}=x_r\phi_r$ and $\phi_r^2=1-\delta^2$. On a generalized joint weight whose adjacent entries differ by neither $1$ nor $-1$, $1-\delta^2$ is invertible by a finite nilpotent geometric series; hence the swapped weight is nonzero. If any entry of a nonzero weight is not integral, move its leftmost nonintegral entry left across all preceding integral entries. The swaps are invertible, but the resulting first entry contradicts $\prod_j(x_1-m_j)=0$. Thus all spectra are integral. For each position separately choose an annihilator $p_r(z)=\prod_{a\in S_r}(z-a)^{N_r}$ from its finite regular spectrum, with $N_r=\dim H_d(m)$ sufficient. Chinese remainder interpolation gives mutually orthogonal polynomial projectors $E_{r,a}(x_r)$ summing to one. Their products $e(i)=\prod_r E_{r,i_r}(x_r)$ give exactly the simultaneous generalized-weight projectors on every finite module; algebra identities follow from regular faithfulness. There is no assertion that the first-position cyclotomic polynomial annihilates other dots.

**The content-block centre comparison.** In an admissible stable realization the actual endomorphism theorem identifies $H:=H^\Lambda_\alpha$ with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(T_\alpha)^{op}$. Choose $Q=T_\alpha\oplus Q_0$, where $Q_0$ is a projective generator of its genuine category-O block, and put $A=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(Q)^{op}$ and $M=\pi Q$. Full faithfulness on projectives identifies $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(Q)$ with $\operatorname{End}_H(M)$, and $M$ contains the regular left module $\pi T_\alpha=H$. No projectivity of all of $M$ over $H$ is assumed.

**The exact centre calculation.** A central endomorphism $z$ of $M$ commutes with the projection onto its direct summand $H$, so it restricts on $H$ to right multiplication $R_h$. Commuting with every $R_b$ forces $h\in Z(H)$. For each $m\in M$, extend the map $f_m:H\to M$, $a\mapsto am$, by zero on the chosen complement of $H$ in $M$. Commutation with this endomorphism gives $zf_m=f_mR_h$; evaluation at one gives $z(m)=hm$. Conversely multiplication by central $h$ commutes with every $H$-map. These constructions are inverse, proving $Z(\operatorname{End}_H M)=Z(H)$, and passage to opposite rings preserves centres. The stated Choice assumption is inherited only for the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers.

**Central content interpolation.** Symmetric polynomials in the dots commute with crossings by the native cross relations, because $s_r$ commutes with $x_r+x_{r+1}$ and $x_rx_{r+1}$ and with all other dots; these generate the elementary symmetric polynomials. Their elementary symmetric values distinguish the finitely many different multisets of generalized joint eigenvalues. Finite Chinese remainder interpolation in these symmetric operators therefore gives a central multiset projector. Its action on every regular generalized weight is one precisely on that multiset, so it equals the orbit sum $e_\alpha$ of the per-position projectors from step 1.1. This argument does not require the annihilating polynomials for different positions to be equal.

**A single linkage block has no split central idempotent.** $\mathcal O_\alpha$ is a single linkage block by [[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]]: it admits no decomposition into two nonzero orthogonal factors. A central idempotent $f=f^2\ne0$ of $A$ with $f\ne1$ would split the projective generator $Q=Qf\oplus Q(1-f)$ into two nonzero summands whose Hom-spaces in both directions vanish, because every morphism between them is annihilated by composing with $f$ on either side in the two possible orders; this exhibits $\mathcal O_\alpha$ as the product of the two nonzero full subcategories generated by these summands, contradicting single-linkage. Hence $Z(A)$ has no nontrivial idempotent, and by step 1.2 the same holds for $Z(H)=Z(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$: the stable content component is a single block.

**Symmetric polynomials in the $x_r$ are central.** It suffices to show that the elementary symmetric functions in the $x_r$ are fixed by conjugation with each basic transposition $s_r$, since these generate the symmetric polynomials and commute with all $x_i$ with $i\notin\{r,r+1\}$. The defining cross relations of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] give $x_{r+1}s_r=s_rx_r+1$ and $s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1$; multiplying the first by $s_r$ on the left yields $s_rx_{r+1}s_r=x_r+s_r$, and the second yields $s_rx_rs_r=x_{r+1}-s_r$. Consequently $s_r(x_r+x_{r+1})s_r=x_r+x_{r+1}$ and $s_r(x_rx_{r+1})s_r=(x_{r+1}-s_r)(x_r+s_r)=x_rx_{r+1}$, so the two elementary generators in the pair $\{x_r,x_{r+1}\}$ are fixed, and $s_r^2=1$ makes the same true for every polynomial in them; together with the commuting generators this fixes every symmetric polynomial. Comparing with step 2.1, $e_\alpha$ commutes with every $x_i$ and every $s_r$, hence is central in $H_d(m)$.

**Arbitrary consecutive $I$.** Let $I$ be any nonempty consecutive set and fix a content $\alpha$ and a finite list of residue operations to be performed. Choose a finite lower endpoint $k$ and an upper endpoint $r$ so that every charge $m_j$ lies in the letter alphabet $[k,r+1]$ and every simple-root support occurring in the list lies in $[k,r]$; enlarge an auxiliary stable realization only in the direction of the stable range, so that the added bottom rows of every tableau are forced to keep the ground entry in every column and every added top entry is absent. By the actual double-cut/common-tail compatibility and the contractible-central-corner restriction of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]] and [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]], the $I$-supported content component $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the same finite-dimensional algebra as the corresponding content component of the stable realization, with the same intrinsic Specht modules, the same residue projectors and the same residue maps; no whole-degree equality is used. Applying step 2.2 to that common component proves (b) for arbitrary consecutive $I$. For a content supported in the original $I$, every auxiliary letter below $I^+$ has its ground multiplicity $l$, the maximum possible in $l$ strict columns, and every auxiliary letter above $I^+$ has multiplicity zero. Thus all added lower entries are present in every column and all added upper entries are absent. If $I$ is finite, deleting that forced common tail leaves only column-strict tableaux in the finite original letter alphabet $I^+$; there are finitely many such tableaux with the fixed column heights. A nonzero supported component has nonzero $T_\alpha$ by the endomorphism identification and hence at least one such tableau label. Thus only finitely many supported contents occur, and the sum of their identities is an identity of the tower. For an infinite interval each element still has finite support in the direct sum, which gives the asserted local units.

**Simple-preserving duality.** In the stable finite realization, the proof paragraph **Simple images and standard heads** of [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]] identifies every Hecke simple with $\pi L(A)$ for a standard label. Restricted category-$\mathcal O$ duality fixes $L(A)$, as recorded in [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]], and the paragraph **The actual duality comparison** of the Whittaker supplier proves $\pi D\cong(\pi-)^{\circledast}$. Hence $(\pi L(A))^{\circledast}\cong\pi DL(A)\cong\pi L(A)$. The intrinsic block identity of step 3.2 preserves the generator-fixing anti-involution, so the same conclusion holds for arbitrary admitted $I$. Commutation with residue functors alone would not establish this simple-preserving assertion.

**Zero components are allowed.** Centrality does not exclude $e_\alpha=0$. Steps 2.2 and 3.2 prove primitivity exactly when the component is nonzero; they do not assert that every positive root content occurs. The stable realization is invoked with precisely the hypotheses declared in the Given.

**Level zero and the vanishing witness.** At level $0$ the cyclotomic polynomial is the empty product $1$, so $H_d(m)=0$ for $d>0$ and only $H_0(m)=\mathbb C$ remains; this is the convention of (2). For the witness, $I=\{0\}$, level $1$, charge $(0)$, $d=2$: the level-one presentation gives $x_1=0$ and $x_2=s_1$, so $H_2(0)=\mathbb C[S_2]$ with eigenvalues $\pm1$ for $x_2$; hence $E_0(x_2)=0$, $e(0,0)=0$, and the supported component $H^\Lambda_{2\alpha_0}=e_{(0,0)}H_2(0)$ is $0$, while $H_2(0)\ne0$. This completes the proof of the two claims (b) and the level-$0$ convention; the exactness and biadjointness clauses of (4) are the declared supplier statements of [[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]], not reproved here.

Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small abelian category in which every object
has finite length. Let $\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)$ be the set of
isomorphism classes of simple objects. The homomorphism

$$\Phi:\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)]\longrightarrow G_0(\mathcal C),\qquad e_{[S]}\longmapsto[S],$$

is an isomorphism. For any object $M$ and simple object $S$, the coordinate of
$[M]$ under $\Phi^{-1}$ at $e_{[S]}$ is $[M:S]$, the number of composition
factors isomorphic to $S$ in a composition series of $M$.

Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal C'$ be essentially small abelian categories and let
$\mathcal D,\mathcal D'$ be essentially small additive categories. For any
abelian group $H$, every function
$\chi\colon\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal C)\to H$ satisfying
$\chi(Y)=\chi(X)+\chi(Z)$ for every short exact sequence
$0\to X\to Y\to Z\to0$ factors uniquely as a homomorphism
$\overline\chi\colon G_0(\mathcal C)\to H$ with
$\overline\chi([X])=\chi(X)$. Every function
$\psi\colon\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal D)\to H$ satisfying
$\psi(X\oplus Y)=\psi(X)+\psi(Y)$ factors uniquely as a homomorphism
$\overline\psi\colon K_0^{\mathrm{split}}(\mathcal D)\to H$ with
$\overline\psi([X])=\psi(X)$. Here $\operatorname{Iso}$ is the set of
isomorphism classes, so these are class functions.

An exact functor between essentially small abelian categories induces a
homomorphism on $G_0$, and an additive functor between essentially small
additive categories induces a homomorphism on split $K_0$. These assignments
preserve identities and composition. Naturally isomorphic exact functors, or
naturally isomorphic additive functors, induce equal homomorphisms.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **The Schur quotient and its simple images.** Assume AC ([F3]) as the imported suppliers do. In the admissible stable realization, the exact Schur quotient $\pi$ of [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]] is the Serre quotient killing exactly the simples $L(A)$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; it satisfies $\pi(N(A))=S(A)$ for the intrinsic Specht modules and $\pi(L(A))=D(A)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, these $D(A)$ being pairwise nonisomorphic and exhausting the simples of $\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)$, while $\pi(L(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$. By [F1] the classes $[D(A)]$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$. The ingredients are the Schur-functor image theorem, exactness of $\pi$ and the double-centralizer/quotient description of [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]].

**The Fock side of the dictionary.** On the Fock side the normalized highest projection $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}$ is the linear map with $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A=D_A$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}M_B=S_B$ with $M_B=\sum_{A}d_{A,B}(s)L_A$ and $S_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)D_A$ at source parameter $1$; the vectors $\{D_A\}$ span the full integral costandard lattice $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ and the vectors $\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ form the standard monomial basis of that lattice, a second integral basis. These are the definitions and the standard-monomial basis theorem of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], together with the O-side dictionary $[L(A)]\mapsto L_A$, $[P(A)]\mapsto P_A$, $[T(A)]\mapsto T_A$ of [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]].

**The O-side Grothendieck group is the integral Fock module.** At parameter one the parabolic category-O Grothendieck group is identified with the integral Fock module by $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$, with $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$ and $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$, by [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]]; here $M(A)$, $L(A)$, $P(A)$ are the generalized standard, simple and projective objects of the genuine block $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].

**The identification of $G_0$ with the costandard lattice.** Define $\Phi\colon G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))\to V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ on the basis of step 1.1 by $\Phi([D(A)])=D_A$. This is a well-defined group isomorphism because both sides are free $\mathbb Z$-modules with the same basis set $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$: on the module side by [F1] and step 1.1, on the Fock side by step 1.2, which exhibits $\{D_A\}$ as a $\mathbb Z$-basis of the FULL integral costandard lattice and makes no integral ground-generation claim. This proves (i) for the simple classes and, together with step 1.2, identifies $\Phi([S(B)])$ with $S_B$.

**The Specht classes.** For the intrinsic Specht module $S(B)=\pi(N(B))$ of step 1.1, apply the exact functor $\pi$ to a Jordan–Hölder composition series of $N(B)$; exactness and [F2] give $[S(B)]=\sum_{A}[N(B):L(A)]\,[D(A)]$ in $G_0$, the sum running over the simples, i.e. over $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ by step 1.1. The multiplicity $[N(B):L(A)]$ equals the Fock coefficient $d_{A,B}(1)$ of step 1.2 by the O-side multiplicity dictionary of step 1.3 and the Schur-image theorem of step 1.1. Hence $\Phi([S(B)])=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)D_A=S_B$, and the square submatrix on standard columns is unitriangular, so $\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ is an integral basis; this completes (i).

**Divided-power integral forms.** The lower library global vectors $G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)=T_{A^\uparrow}=s^{-a(\alpha)}P_A$ and the form-dual upper vectors $G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a(\alpha)}D_A$ with $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$ span integral forms on which the divided powers of the Chevalley generators act integrally, by [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; at parameter one the standard lattice is therefore generated over $\mathbb Z$ by its ground vector $P_{A_\Lambda}$ under the divided-power operators $f_i^{(n)}$, while the costandard lattice is its full weightwise $C_0$-dual: at $s=1$, $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ identifies it with $\bigoplus_\alpha\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z,\alpha},\mathbb Z)$. In particular it is stable under divided powers, since the $e_i^{(n)}$ and $f_i^{(n)}$ are adjoint and preserve the lower lattice. Nondegeneracy identifies their rational scalar extensions, but does not identify the two integral lattices. The ground-generation use is the actual definition $V_{\mathcal A}(\Lambda)=U^-_{\mathcal A}v_\Lambda$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], specialized at one; it concerns the standard lattice only. This gives the divided-power clause of (ii) and separates the two lattices.

**Residue operators.** The residue functors $e_i^H,f_i^H$ are exact, so they induce endomorphisms of $G_0$ by [F2]. The natural intertwining isomorphisms $f_i^H\pi\cong\pi f_i^O$ and $e_i^H\pi\cong\pi e_i^O$ of [[thm-category-o-translation-intertwines-residue-induction-and-restriction]], together with the category-O Chevalley action of [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]], show that $[\pi]$ is a module map. Steps 1.1–2.2 identify its kernel with the span of the off-standard simple classes, precisely the kernel of the Fock projection. Thus the induced quotient map $\Phi$ intertwines $e_i,f_i$, proving the ordinary Chevalley clause of (ii). No head, socle or indecomposability assertion is inferred merely from exactness of a quotient.

**Level zero.** If the level is $0$, then $\Lambda=0$, the only simple is the ground class in degree $0$, and the tower is $H^\Lambda_0=\mathbb C$ by the level-$0$ convention of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]; then $G_0=\mathbb Z[D(\varnothing)]\cong\mathbb ZD_\varnothing$ is the ground line alone, with both lattices equal to the ground line and every residue operator zero. This is the level-$0$ clause of (v).

**Crystal reachability and composition factors.** The source upper ground component is exactly $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ by [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]]. The normalized highest form is nondegenerate on each finite weight space, so over $\mathbb Q$ it identifies the full costandard lattice's scalar extension with the irreducible highest module. Its highest vector therefore generates that module under lowering divided powers. Consequently every basis vector $D_A$ is a rational linear combination of lowering words applied to the ground vector. By step 3.1 each ordinary lowering word is the class of the corresponding exact residue-word module, with nonnegative simple-class coefficients by [F1]. If $D(A)$ occurred in none of these modules, every such word and every rational linear combination would have zero $D_A$ coefficient, contrary to the coefficient one in $D_A$. Thus some residue word contains $D(A)$ as a composition factor. This proves (iv) without requiring integral costandard generation or transport of head and socle through the quotient.

**The maps for arbitrary consecutive $I$.** Fix a finite set of contents and residue words. Choose $J=[k,r]$ so that $[k,r+1]$ contains every charge and $J$ contains every intermediate root support; decrease $k$ further to reach the needed stable range. The Hecke-side map is literally the identity on $H_d(m)e_\alpha$: its spectral idempotent is the same sum over words of content $\alpha$, independently of whether the ambient supported interval is $I$ or $J$. It therefore fixes the intrinsic residue corner $u_{\alpha,i}$ and the bimodules defining $e_i,f_i$. On tableaux the lower transition adjoins the prescribed ground entries to every column, and the upper transition regards the same entries in a larger alphabet with no new top entries. Removing that common tail is the inverse on the selected weight. Column ground differences, hence intrinsic Specht partitions, are unchanged. The actual finite-cut compatibility of [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]] and [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]] gives $D_{\jmath A}=\jmath D_A$, $S_{\jmath B}=\jmath S_B$, $P_{\jmath A}=\jmath P_A$ and commuting normalized highest projections. Thus both upper and lower lattices are identified by their full bases, not just their rational spans. On overlapping cuts these maps compose by adjoining/removing the same ground entries and by the intrinsic Hecke identity; the normalized projections agree by highest-vector uniqueness. Every content, vector and finite residue word fits such a cut. Applying the bounded-below identifications and the rational-cyclicity argument of steps 1.1–4.1 there, and taking the compatible weightwise direct sum, proves all clauses for arbitrary admitted $I$. No full degree algebra is identified with a proper supported cut.

**Rational ground cyclicity.** The normalized $E/F$-contravariant highest form is nondegenerate on each finite weight space. Thus its weightwise duality identifies $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Q}$, interpreted as the direct sum of the costandard weight spaces, with the irreducible rational highest module. The ground vector maps to the normalized highest vector; its orbit under lowering divided powers therefore spans every weight space, as used in step 4.1. This proves the rational clause of (iii). The full unrestricted algebraic dual of an infinite-dimensional module is not used.

**The rank-one index-two witness.** Take $I=\{0\}$ and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$. The supported degree-one block is $B_0=\mathbb C[x]/x^2$ and the supported degree-two block is $M_2(\mathbb C)$, with its simple represented by $x_1=N=E_{12}$, $s_1=-(E_{12}+E_{21})$ and $x_2=-N$. For completeness the whole degree-two presentation gives an isomorphism $H_2(0,0)\cong M_2(\mathbb C)\oplus B_+\oplus B_-$ with $B_\pm=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$: send $(x_1,x_2,s_1)$ to $(N,-N,-J)$ in the matrix factor and to $(\epsilon,\pm1+\epsilon,\pm1)$ in the other factors. The eight PBW spanning words are $1,x_1,x_2,x_1x_2,s_1,x_1s_1,x_2s_1,x_1x_2s_1$. The central sum $z=x_1+x_2$ has spectra $0,1,-1$ on the three factors; its Hermite polynomials $(1-z^2)^2$ and $\{1-(1-z^2)^2\pm(3z-z^3)/2\}/2$ project onto the three factors. Each factor is generated by the images, making the map onto an eight-dimensional product surjective and hence an isomorphism by the spanning bound. The all-zero-residue cut is exactly the matrix factor. In degree three an all-zero-residue module would have $x_2=-x_1$, $x_1^2=0$ from the matrix factor; $s_2$ commutes with $x_1$ and therefore with $x_2$, so $x_3=s_2x_2s_2+s_2=x_2+s_2$ has eigenvalues $\pm1$, contradiction. The same argument excludes all higher degrees. The first dot is not zero on the matrix simple. Induction from degree zero gives the regular $B_0$-module, with two simple factors. The matrix algebra is right-free of rank two over $B_0$ under $x\mapsto N$, so induction of its one-dimensional simple has dimension two and is the matrix simple; restricting that matrix simple gives the regular $B_0$-module. Restricting the degree-one simple to degree zero has dimension one. Thus the residue Ind/Res computations give $fD_{00}=2D_{01}$, $fD_{01}=D_{11}$ and $eD_{01}=D_{00}$, $eD_{11}=2D_{01}$, with the end actions zero. Their divided squares give $f^{(2)}D_{00}=D_{11}$ and $e^{(2)}D_{11}=D_{00}$. Therefore $\mathbb ZD_{00}\oplus2\mathbb ZD_{01}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{11}$ is stable under $e,f$ and all their divided powers, contains the ground vector and excludes $D_{01}$. This is a proper integral costandard submodule, whereas over $\mathbb Q$ division by two recovers $D_{01}$. Degree one is not called a corner sitting inside degree two.

$S_1,\ldots,S_t$ for representatives of the isomorphism classes of simple
left $A$-modules, and choose a finite-dimensional projective cover
$q_i\colon P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ for each $i$. Then the split
Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional projective left $A$-modules
([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]]) is the free abelian
group with basis $[P_1],\ldots,[P_t]$. In particular, each selected cover is
indecomposable, the $P_i$ are pairwise nonisomorphic, and every finite
dimensional projective is a finite direct sum of them. This result makes no
claim that the Cartan map to the short-exact-sequence group $G_0(A)$ is
invertible.

Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital associative $k$-algebra. Let $S_1,\ldots,S_t$ represent all isomorphism classes of simple left $A$-modules, and let $q_i:P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ be finite-dimensional projective covers. Then $[P_1],\ldots,[P_t]$ and $[S_1],\ldots,[S_t]$ are bases of $K_0(A)$ and $G_0(A)$, respectively, and $$\langle[P_i],[S_j]\rangle_A=\begin{cases}\dim_k\operatorname{End}_A(S_i),&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j.\end{cases}$$ In particular, if $\operatorname{End}_A(S_i)=k$ for every $i$, these bases are dual.

For a finite-dimensional unital associative $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebra, let $S_1,\ldots,S_t$ represent the graded-simple shift orbits and let $p_i:P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ be finite graded projective covers. Here graded-simple means nonzero with no proper nonzero graded submodule. Then $[P_i]$ and $[S_i]$ are $R=\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$-bases of $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$ and $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$, respectively, and $$\langle[P_i],[S_j]\rangle_{A,\mathrm{gr}}=\begin{cases}\dim_k\operatorname{End}_{A,0}(S_i),&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j.\end{cases}$$ If $\operatorname{End}_{A,0}(S_i)=k$ for every representative, these Laurent bases are dual. Neither pairing statement asserts unimodularity of the projective-to-module Cartan map or of a projective/projective Cartan matrix. No axiom of choice is assumed or used.

finite-dimensional projective left $A$-module $P$ and finite-dimensional left
$A$-module $M$, define the object-level value

$$h(P,M):=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,M).$$

If $A$ is $\mathbb Z$-graded and $P,M$ are finite-dimensional graded left $A$-modules,
with $P$ projective in the degree-zero graded category, define

$$h_{\mathrm{gr}}(P,M):=\sum_{d\in\mathbb Z}v^d\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,M),$$

where $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,M)$ consists of $A$-linear maps sending each

Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small abelian category in which every object
has finite length. Let $\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)$ be the set of
isomorphism classes of simple objects. The homomorphism

$$\Phi:\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)]\longrightarrow G_0(\mathcal C),\qquad e_{[S]}\longmapsto[S],$$

is an isomorphism. For any object $M$ and simple object $S$, the coordinate of
$[M]$ under $\Phi^{-1}$ at $e_{[S]}$ is $[M:S]$, the number of composition
factors isomorphic to $S$ in a composition series of $M$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$
be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). The **arbitrary-level
cyclotomic Hecke algebra** $H_n=H_n(R;z;U_1,\dots,U_\ell)$ is the $R$-algebra
presented by invertible commuting elements $X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ subject to the relations
$$(T_i-z)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$
$$T_iX_iT_i=zX_{i+1},\qquad X_jT_i=T_iX_j\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad \prod_{a=1}^{\ell}(X_1-U_a)=0 .$$
For $n=0$ set $H_0=R$. The **grading variable** of this page is $v$, not the
unit $z$: the two are identified only where a statement says so explicitly.

**Multipartitions and Murphy data.** An $\ell$-**multipartition** of $n$ is an
ordered tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\dots,\lambda^{(\ell)})$ of partitions
with $\sum_{b}|\lambda^{(b)}|=n$ ([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]).
Multipartitions are partially ordered by dominance, $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ meaning
that $\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\lambda^{(k)}_j\ge
\sum_{b<k}|\mu^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\mu^{(k)}_j$ for all $k,m$. Fill the
diagram $t^\lambda$ with $1,\dots,n$ in component order, then row order, then
column order. Put $a_k:=\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|$,
$u_\lambda:=\prod_{k=1}^{\ell}\prod_{j\le a_k}(X_j-U_k)$,
$x_\lambda:=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and $m_\lambda:=x_\lambda u_\lambda$,
where $S_\lambda$ is the row subgroup: the subgroup of $S_n$ stabilizing the
rows of $t^\lambda$
([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]],
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Write $M_\lambda:=m_\lambda H_n$ for
the right $H_n$-submodule generated by $m_\lambda$
([[def-left-and-right-modules]]). The **presentation involution** $*$ of $H_n$
fixes every $X_j$ and every $T_i$ and reverses products. For standard
tableaux $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$ put $m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^{*}m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$,
where the right tableau action is $t\cdot w:=w^{-1}\cdot t$ (the left action relabels entries), and $d(s)$ is determined by $t^\lambda\cdot d(s)=s$.
Denote by $H^{>\lambda}$ the span of the higher Murphy shapes once their
basis and cell law is established by
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]], and by
$S_\lambda$ the right cell (**Specht**) module with basis $m_t$ and the
action given by that cell law; its cellular form defines
$D_\lambda:=S_\lambda/\operatorname{rad}S_\lambda$, which may vanish.

**Types.** The types used below are **exactly** all $\ell$-multipartitions of
$n$, including tuples with empty components — not all multicompositions. A
**semistandard tableau** $S$ has entries the labels $(i,k)$ (row $i$ in
component $k$) ordered by component first and then by row, weakly increasing
along rows, strictly increasing down columns, and a label of component $a$
may occur only in physical component $b\le a$
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]); the **type** of $S$ is the
multipartition counting each label with the multiplicity of the corresponding
row. For standard $s$ let $\mu(s)$ be the tableau obtained from $s$ by
replacing each entry by its row-and-component in $t^{\mu}$. Put
$$m_{(S,t)}:=\sum_{s:\,\mu(s)=S}m_{st},\qquad m_{(S,T)}:=\sum_{s,t:\,\mu(s)=S,\ \nu(t)=T}m_{st}.$$
Let
$$M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\ \text{multipartition of}\ n}M_\lambda,\qquad C_n:=\operatorname{End}_{H_n}(M),$$
with ordinary composition ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]). For
$S,T$ of shape $\lambda$ and types $\mu,\nu$, the map $\varphi_{ST}$ — once
justified by [[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] —
sends $m_\alpha h$ to $\delta_{\alpha,\nu}m_{(S,T)}h$. Its right cell module
$\Delta_\lambda$ has basis $v_T$ over the semistandard $T$ of multipartition
types, with contravariant cell form and quotient $L_\lambda$. Let $T^\lambda$
be the unique tableau of shape and type $\lambda$, and let $e_\lambda$ be the
identity projection onto $M_\lambda$. Put $\omega:=(\varnothing,\dots,\varnothing,(1^n))$
and $e:=e_\omega$; then $m_\omega=1$, so $M_\omega=H_n$, and $H_n$ is an
actual direct summand of $M$. The weight projections used by the Jantzen
theory below are the $e_\nu$ with $\nu$ a multipartition. Write
$K_{(\lambda,\nu)}:=\#\operatorname{SStd}_\nu(\lambda)$ for the number of
semistandard tableaux of shape $\lambda$ and type $\nu$.

**Boundary of the definition.** All asserted module, form and map laws are
discharged by the linked local suppliers
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]],
[[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] and
[[thm-cyclotomic-schur-standards-and-schur-functor-control-block-linkage]];
the definition itself claims no proof of them and no primitive
residue-content classification. No choice principle is used: only finite
bases, finite subgroup and coset decompositions, finite filtrations and
explicit polynomial identities occur.

On the Specht module $S_\lambda$ of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]], $X_r$
acts dominance-triangularly with diagonal $U_az^{j-i}$ at the node $(i,j,a)$
carrying $r$. Over a field with $z=q_H$ of finite order $e\ge2$ and
$U_a=q_H^{c_a}$, every simultaneous generalized eigenword of $S_\lambda$ is
among the standard-tableau residue words $c_a+j-i$ modulo $e$; every such word
has the fixed node-residue multiplicities of $\lambda$. The universal
triangularity also specializes to the LM deformation DVR and the generic
fibre, with no semisimplicity or affine-center premise.

$\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ be the Schur functor of
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]],
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Use the current category-O namespace:
$N(A):=M(A)$ is the generalized standard, $K(A):=\nabla(A)$ the costandard,
$L(A)$ the category-O simple and $P(A)$ its projective cover, as in
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
The source17 symbol $K(A)$ denotes our $L(A)$, not our costandard $K(A)$.
Write $\mathsf L(A):=\mathrm{Wh}(L(A))$ for the finite-W image of the
category-O simple; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ this is the source finite-W simple
appearing in the Whittaker/Morita contract of
[[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]].
In particular the $W_d$-Hom below takes a finite-W module as its second
argument. Let $\mathrm{Std}$ be the standard labels. Then:

1. For every label $A$, the Schur image of the standard object $N(A)$ is the
   intrinsic affine-induced Specht module
   $$S(A)=H_d\otimes_{H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}}\Bigl(\bigotimes_j \mathrm{ev}^*_{a_j}S^{\mu^{(j)}}\Bigr),\qquad a_j=c_j+q_j-n,$$
   where $\mu^{(j)}$ is the partition of $d_j$ read from the nonnegative
   ground differences in the $j$-th column of $A$ and the factors are induced
   along the affine Young subalgebra $H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}=H_{d_1}\otimes\cdots
   \otimes H_{d_l}$. Its affine action factors through the cyclotomic image $B_d$, so the same module is obtained by replacing $H_d$ in this tensor product by $H_d(\mathbf a)$.
2. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ the module
   $D(A)=\pi(L(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},\mathsf L(A))$ is
   simple, the modules $D(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, form a complete set of
   pairwise non-isomorphic simples of the Hecke image $B_d$, and
   $\pi(L(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}$.
3. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, $\pi(P(A))$ is the projective cover $Y(A)$ of
   $D(A)$, and $\pi^*\pi(P(A))\cong P(A)$; ambient off-standard projectives
   still have their genuine images, and no projective-preservation assertion
   is made for them.
4. Images of tiltings carry the opposite-parabolic standard/Specht flag
   coefficients, and $\pi$ is fully faithful on tiltings.
5. For $A\in\mathrm{Col}$ and $B\in\mathrm{Std}$,
   $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):L(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$, where $d_{B,A}$ is the typed
   canonical-basis coefficient of the Fock-space dictionary; for $B\notin
   \mathrm{Std}$ the symbol $D(B)$ is not a Hecke simple. All interfaces are
   ungraded at parameter $1$.

Work over the field $\mathbb C$ and fix an integer $d\ge 0$
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], [[def-commutative-ring]]). Let
$\mathcal F_d$ be the free associative unital $\mathbb C$-algebra on the
$d+\max(d-1,0)$ symbols $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ (for $d=0$ there is only
the unit; for $d=1$ only $x_1$), with its word basis and universal property
([[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]]), and let
$I_d\mathrel{\trianglelefteq}\mathcal F_d$ be the two-sided ideal
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]])
generated by the following elements:

- $x_ix_j-x_jx_i$ for all $1\le i,j\le d$;
- $s_i^2-1$, $s_is_{i+1}s_i-s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1}$, and $s_is_j-s_js_i$ for
  $|i-j|>1$, for $1\le i,j\le d-1$;
- $s_ix_j-x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$, $s_ix_{i+1}-x_is_i-1$, and
  $x_{i+1}s_i-s_ix_i-1$, for $1\le i\le d-1$ and $1\le j\le d$.

The **degenerate affine Hecke algebra** is the quotient $\mathbb C$-algebra
$$H_d:=\mathcal F_d/I_d$$
with unit element written $1$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]). We keep the symbols
$x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ for their images, and for $w\in S_d$ we write
$w$ for the image in $H_d$ of any word in the $s_i$ representing $w$; this is
independent of the chosen word once the basis theorem below is proved. For
$d\ge1$ and $a\in\mathbb C$, the notation $H_d/(x_1-a)$ means the quotient by the two-sided
ideal generated by $x_1-a$.

The verification below establishes exactly the structure of $H_d$ used
throughout this page: the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad r_1,\dots,r_d\ge0,\ w\in S_d,$$
form a $\mathbb C$-basis, so that
$H_d\cong\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[S_d]$ as a vector
space with polynomial and group-algebra subalgebras
([[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]], [[def-group-ring]]);
$H_0=\mathbb C$ and $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$; for $d\ge1$ and every $a$ there is a unique
algebra isomorphism
$$H_d/(x_1-a)\cong\mathbb C[S_d],\qquad x_j\longmapsto a+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j);$$
and total polynomial degree is an algebra filtration whose associated graded is
the semidirect product $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$ in which
$s_i$ acts by swapping $x_i$ and $x_{i+1}$. For $d\ge2$, the cross relation is
inhomogeneous, so it does not turn $H_d$ into a graded algebra with
$\deg x_i=1$ and $\deg s_i=0$. For $d=0$ the algebra $\mathbb C$ has its
degree-zero grading, and for $d=1$ the algebra $\mathbb C[x_1]$ has its
natural polynomial grading.

Let $n\ge1$. (a) The elements $X_1,\dots,X_n$ act diagonally in the Young
basis of the previous item: for every standard tableau $T$ of size $n$ and
every $k$, $X_kv_T=c_T(k)v_T$, and the joint eigenspaces are
one-dimensional, indexed by the standard tableaux. (b) A vector
$\alpha=(a_1,\dots,a_n)\in\mathbb Z^n$ occurs as the joint eigenvalue vector
of a $v_T$, equivalently $\alpha=\operatorname{Cont}(T)$ for a standard
tableau $T$, if and only if: (1) $a_1=0$; (2) for every $q>1$ at least one of
$a_q-1,a_q+1$ occurs among $a_1,\dots,a_{q-1}$; (3) if $a_p=a_q$ with $p<q$,
then both $a_p-1$ and $a_p+1$ occur among $a_{p+1},\dots,a_{q-1}$. The
association $T\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(T)$ is a bijection from the standard
tableaux of size $n$ onto this set.

**(i)** The assignment $[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ is an isomorphism from the split

**(ii)** Under the identifications (i) and

**(iii)** The Cartan Hom pairing becomes the normalized highest pairing: with
the projected simple vectors $D_B=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_B$ one has

**(iv)** Both residue functors $e_i$ and $f_i$ on projective modules induce

**(v)** The left adjoint $\pi^*$ of the Schur quotient is right exact on all

derivations.claim: **The two charts are mutually inverse.** By [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] the vectors $L_B$ and $M_A$ are two $\mathbb Z[s,s^{-1}]$-bases of the finite weight spaces of the Fock module, so the transition matrices $R(s)=(p_{A,B}(-s))$ with $L_B=\sum_AR_{A,B}(s)M_A$ and $D(s)=(d_{A,B})$ with $M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A$ satisfy $R(s)D(s)=D(s)R(s)=1$; both are triangular with diagonal entries $1$ on each weight block, and the quasi-canonical vector is $P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$. **The type-$A$ polynomial dictionary.** The explicit transition coefficients are given by the type-$A$ formulas of [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]]: for the right place action, $w_A$ is the shortest sorting element on the RIGHT of the entry stabilizer $K$, $d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ is shortest on the LEFT, $p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,w_B}(s^{-2})$, the column Levi $J$ is distinct from $K$, and the mixed singular/parabolic composition coefficient is the finite Levi cancellation sum $\sum_C(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1)$.

**The O-side multiplicity dictionary.** On the category-O side the standard module $N(B)$ has a composition series whose multiplicities with respect to the simples $L(A)$ are read off in the same chart: the coefficient of $M_B$ in the expansion of $P_A$ is the multiplicity of $L(A)$ in $N(B)$ at parameter one, in the source's reciprocal convention, by [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]] and [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; combined with step 1.1 this gives $[N(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$ for all $A,B$, with $d_{A,B}$ unitriangular, and $[N(B):L(B)]=1$ for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ in the full square matrix.

**Transfer to the Hecke side.** By [F2] the Schur quotient is exact, sends $N(B)$ to $S(B)$, $L(A)$ to $D(A)$ for standard $A$ and kills the off-standard simples; applying it to a composition series of $N(B)$ and using [F1] gives $[S(B):D(A)]=[N(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, the sum being finite on each weight block. This proves (i).

**Shape of the matrix.** The full matrix $D=(d_{A,B})$ is unitriangular on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ by step 1.1; restricting rows to the simple labels $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ (all of which occur, and which index the simples by [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]]) leaves a rectangular matrix, whose square submatrix on the standard columns is again unitriangular with diagonal entries $1$. Off standard columns the equation $D(B)=0$ says precisely that $D(B)$ is not a simple module label, so the identity $[S(B):D(B)]=1$ is asserted only for $B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$. This proves (ii). The statement is not that the rectangular matrix is invertible, and no off-standard simple is created.

**The polynomial coefficient is not a transposed inverse.** In the coefficient convention used in the proof, the decomposition array has rows the simple labels and columns the Specht labels, and its entries are the coefficients of $D(s)$ at $s=1$; since $R(s)=D(s)^{-1}$, its transpose is $D(s)^{-t}$, which is in general different from the $L$-in-$M$ chart $R(s)$. On the two-factor space with labels $01<10$ one has $L_{10}=M_{10}-sM_{01}$, so $R_{01,10}=-s$ is the negative-entry chart, whereas its inverse has $D_{01,10}=s$, while the true decomposition entry is $d_{01,10}(1)=1$: $S(10)$ is the simple $D(01)$ and not a formal negative combination. Hence with simple rows and Specht columns the decomposition matrix is the standard-row restriction of $D$; with Specht rows and simple columns it is its transpose. Neither convention uses the transpose of $R$. This completes (iii) together with steps 1.2, whose entry stabilizer $K$ and column Levi $J$ remain distinct and whose multiplicities are the finite Levi cancellation values at parameter one; all statements are ungraded.

For every $n\ge0$ and $\lambda\vdash n$ the complex Specht module $S^\lambda$
carries a nondegenerate symmetric $S_n$-invariant bilinear form
$$b(x,y)=\sum_T x_Ty_T$$
given by the coefficientwise product in the tabloid basis, so
$v\mapsto b(v,-)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbb C S_n$-modules
$S^\lambda\to(S^\lambda)^*$; equivalently $S^\lambda$ is self-dual.
Consequently $\chi^\lambda(g^{-1})=\chi^\lambda(g)$ for every $g\in S_n$, that
is, every irreducible character of $S_n$ is real-valued.

Let $F$ be a field, $n\ge0$, $\lambda\vdash n$, and let $\lambda'$ be the
conjugate partition. Write $\Omega_\lambda$ for the finite set of
$\lambda$-tabloids and let
$$M^\lambda_F=F^{(\Omega_\lambda)},\qquad S^\lambda_F\subseteq M^\lambda_F,\qquad \kappa_t=\sum_{\gamma\in C_t}\operatorname{sgn}(\gamma)\gamma,\qquad e_t=\kappa_t\{t\}$$
be the field-valued tabloid module, the span of the polytabloids inside it,
the column antisymmetrizer, and the polytabloid of a $\lambda$-tableau $t$
([[def-young-subgroup-tabloid-and-permutation-module]],
[[def-column-antisymmetrizer-polytabloid-and-specht-module]]). Let
$$\beta_F:M^\lambda_F\times M^\lambda_F\longrightarrow F$$
be the $F$-bilinear form for which the tabloid basis is orthonormal
([[def-integral-tabloid-bilinear-form-and-specht-gram-matrix]]), and for a
subspace $V\subseteq M^\lambda_F$ put
$$V^\perp:=\{x\in M^\lambda_F:\beta_F(x,v)=0\text{ for all }v\in V\}.$$

$F w$, so that $\sigma\cdot w=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)w$
([[def-sign-representation-and-restriction-of-a-representation]]), and let
$$S^\lambda_F\otimes\operatorname{sgn}$$
be the tensor product of $F[S_n]$-modules with the diagonal action
$\sigma\cdot(x\otimes w):=(\sigma\cdot x)\otimes(\sigma\cdot w)$, a
finite-dimensional $F[S_n]$-module
([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]). For a
finite-dimensional $F[S_n]$-module $D$ the **dual** is
$D^*=\operatorname{Hom}_F(D,F)$ with $(\sigma\cdot f)(v):=f(\sigma^{-1}v)$.

block $B_i=\{\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_{i-1}+1,\dots,\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_i\}$
in increasing order, and let $t_0^{\mathsf T}$ be its transpose, a

$$\theta(\{u\}):=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma_u)\,\bigl(e_{u^{\mathsf T}}\otimes w\bigr) \ \in\ S^\lambda_F\otimes\operatorname{sgn}.$$

**Lemma.** With this notation:

1. $\theta$ does not depend on the chosen representative $u$ of the tabloid
   $\{u\}$; it is a well-defined $F[S_n]$-module homomorphism
   $\theta:M^{\lambda'}_F\to S^\lambda_F\otimes\operatorname{sgn}$ with
   $\theta(\{t_0^{\mathsf T}\})=e_{t_0}\otimes w$.
2. $\theta$ is surjective and
   $\ker\theta=(S^{\lambda'}_F)^\perp$.

   the second being the composite with $x\mapsto\beta_F(x,\cdot)|_{S^{\lambda'}_F}$.

and set $a_b=c_b+q_b-n$ and $\Lambda=\sum_{b=1}^l\Lambda_{a_b}$, with a

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $x_1,\dots,x_r$ be an ordered basis of a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. Then the monomials

$$x_1^{a_1}x_2^{a_2}\cdots x_r^{a_r} \qquad (a_i\in \mathbb N_0)$$

form a basis of $U(\mathfrak g)$. In particular, multiplication identifies $\operatorname{gr}U(\mathfrak g)$ with the symmetric algebra $S(\mathfrak g)$ on the symbols of the $x_i$.

Every finite-dimensional representation of a finite-dimensional semisimple
Lie algebra over any characteristic-zero field is completely reducible.

derivations.claim: **The sign automorphism.** The assignments $\sigma(s_r)=-s_r$ and $\sigma(x_r)=-x_r$ respect the defining relations of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]: involution and braid relations hold for the $s_r$ and the $x_r$ commute, and the cross relation $s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1$ is preserved because the two minus signs in each product cancel and $1$ is fixed, while $x_{r+1}s_r=s_rx_r+1$ is preserved the same way. Hence $\sigma$ is an algebra automorphism of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra; it maps the polynomial idempotent $e(i)$ to $e(-i)$ and therefore the block idempotent $e_\alpha$ of $H_d(m)$ to the block idempotent $e_{\alpha^t}$ of $H_d(m^t)$, giving an isomorphism $H^\Lambda_\alpha\cong H^{\Lambda^t}_{\alpha^t}$ that intertwines the tower inclusion and the residue projectors $u_{\alpha,i}$ with $u_{\alpha^t,-i}$; twisting modules by $\sigma$ gives exact functors that interchange residue $i$ with residue $-i$ and commute with the duality $\circledast$ (which is defined by the $x_r$- and $s_r$-fixed anti-automorphism and is therefore $\sigma$-stable).

**The transpose of multipartitions.** Write $\lambda^{(j)}_r=A(m_j+1-r,j)-(m_j+1-r)$; these ground differences give a partition in each column. Reversing components and transposing the partitions is an involution. A node $(r,c)$ in component $j$ has residue $m_j+c-r$; its transposed node has residue $-m_j+r-c$, so the content becomes $\alpha^t$. For adjacent charges put $g=m_j-m_{j+1}\ge0$, $\lambda=\lambda^{(j)}$ and $\mu=\lambda^{(j+1)}$. The aligned reverse-standard row inequalities are $\lambda_r+g\ge\mu_r$ for all $r$, whereas standard rows in the reflected shape require $\mu^{\mathsf T}_{a+g}\le\lambda^{\mathsf T}_a$ for all $a\ge1$. These conditions are equivalent: the first makes every row of $\mu$ of length at least $a+g$ a row of $\lambda$ of length at least $a$; conversely, if $\mu_r>\lambda_r+g$, take $a=\lambda_r+1$ to get $\mu^{\mathsf T}_{a+g}\ge r>\lambda^{\mathsf T}_a$. Applying this to every adjacent pair proves the bijection $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Std}^{\Lambda^t}_{\alpha^t}$, with inverse the same reversed-component transpose.

**Full faithfulness on all projectives and tiltings.** In the admissible stable realization the exact Schur quotient $\pi$ is fully faithful on ALL category-O projectives and on all tilting objects, the endomorphism isomorphism identifies the Hecke image algebra with the endomorphism algebra of the prinjective detector, and the category-O tilting objects are classified with a standard flag, by [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]], [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]], [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]] and [[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]]; the Young and signed-Young images are the ones of [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]] and [[thm-type-a-parabolic-category-o-ringel-duality-via-the-opposite-parabolic]]. The tilting faithfulness use is the local head/socle corner argument: a standard flag gives standard socle labels and duality gives standard head labels; the unit into the right adjoint of the corner is injective with corner-killed cokernel, and a module with only standard head labels has no nonzero map into such a cokernel. Adjunction therefore lifts every corner map uniquely. This argument uses both flags, rather than claiming that exactness alone preserves heads.

**Longest-shuffle induction duality.** Let $P$ be the affine Young subalgebra with original block sizes and $Q$ the reversed block subalgebra. Affine PBW on the right gives $H_d=\bigoplus_{u\in U}uP$, where $U$ consists of minimal right coset representatives. Its unique longest representative $r$ reverses the blocks, preserving their internal orders; its length is the number of cross-block pairs. Let $\theta:Q\to P$ relabel positions by $r^{-1}$ and let $E(\sum up_u)=p_r$. Then $E$ is right $P$-linear and $E(qh)=\theta(q)E(h)$. Indeed straightening $x_ju$ gives $ux_{u^{-1}j}$ plus shorter-permutation terms, which cannot reach the longest coset, and an internal $Q$ reflection preserves that coset with $s_jr=r\theta(s_j)$. For finite $P$-module $M$, give $M^*$ its generator-fixing dual action and transport it to $Q$ through $\theta$. The pairing $\langle a\otimes m,b\otimes\varphi\rangle=\varphi(E(b^*a)m)$ is balanced by these two identities and is contravariant.

Minimal representatives $v$ for $H_d/Q$ satisfy $vr\in U$; $E(v^{-1}u)$ is one precisely when $u=vr$ and zero otherwise. Thus the pairing matrix is a permutation matrix tensored with the ordinary perfect pairing, proving that the dual of induction is the reverse-block induction of the dual.

**The correctly normalized exterior quotient.** Choose a sufficiently low finite cut $k$, put $q_i=m_i+1-k$, $n=q_1$ and $c=n+k-1$. The ordinary parabolic ground has scalar $q_1+\cdots+q_{i-1}+m_i$, obtained from the head character $-\rho_i=\sum_{j\le i}q_j-n$ plus $c$. The finite-W tail shift is a different embedding convention and is not substituted for this character; the transported roots are nevertheless exactly $m_i=c+q_i-n$. For the transposed component partitions $\nu^{(i)}=(\lambda^{(i)})^{\mathsf T}$ form the exterior suffix module $D=\mathbb C_c\otimes\bigotimes_{i=l}^1\bigwedge^{\nu^{(i)}}(V/V_{i-1})$. Its tensor quotient $q:U=\mathbb C_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}\to D$ is parabolic-linear and hence finite-W-linear. Select $d$ distinct longest row names with idempotent $e_S$ and cyclic rightmost-row tensor $w$; regular evaluation identifies $H\to e_SU$, $b\mapsto wb$, with left corner action $a(wb)=w(ab)$. **An explicit trace-adjoint covector.** Positions have nonincreasing original column types $t_1\ge\cdots\ge t_d$, constant inside exterior blocks $J$. Put $p=\prod_j\prod_{i<t_j}(x_j-m_i)$, $a_-=\sum_{u\in J}\operatorname{sgn}(u)u$ and $g=pa_-=a_-p=g^*$. The native right dot formula on row tensors of columns $c_j$ is $vx_j=v_{L_j}+m_{c_j}v+\sum_{h<j,c_h\ge c_j}v(hj)-\sum_{h>j,c_h<c_j}v(jh)$. Let $\phi_0$ select the all-column-one tensor with fixed row order. Process the factors of $p$ in order $j=1,\ldots,d$, then $i=1,\ldots,t_j-1$. At that stage the target columns are $t_h$ for $h<j$, $i$ at $j$, and one for $h>j$. Transposing the dot formula has no earlier swap, since $t_h\ge t_j>i$, and no later swap, since $1\le i$; its diagonal is $m_i-m_i=0$. It therefore raises exactly that column by one with coefficient one. Thus $\phi_0R_p=\phi_{\mathbf t}$. The covector $\phi_{\mathbf t}R_{a_-}$ alternates inside each exterior block and vanishes on forbidden columns, so equals $\lambda q$ for an actual exterior covector $\lambda$.

**Descent to the projected lattices at parameter one.** At parameter one the simple classes are the projected vectors $D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$ and the projective classes are $P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}$ by [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; the sign and transpose maps of steps 1.1-1.2 act on these two families by the label rules $A\mapsto A^\downarrow$ for costandard vectors on $\mathrm{Rev}$ and by the inverse rectification for standard vectors, compatibly with the identification of [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]]. This is the projected-lattice statement of the first paragraph; the map is not asserted to permute all monomials or all simple labels of the full Fock space, since the off-standard monomials have no simple image.

**The signed full generator and Ringel duality.** Likewise put $\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A):=\pi T_{\mathcal O}(A)$ for every $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$. Full faithfulness on tiltings (step 1.3) makes the full sum $\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}}=\bigoplus_A\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A)$ satisfy $\operatorname{End}_{H^\Lambda}(\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}})^{op}\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(\bigoplus_AT_{\mathcal O}(A))^{op}$, and the characteristic-tilting endomorphism algebra is the Ringel dual of the Schur-cover algebra, realized as the reversed-Levi/opposite-parabolic block via the functor $F=D\Psi$ with its explicit reverse-column shifts and $F(\overline P(A))=T_{\mathcal O}(A)$, by [[thm-type-a-parabolic-category-o-ringel-duality-via-the-opposite-parabolic]], [[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]] and [[def-the-ringel-dual-of-a-finite-highest-weight-ideal]]. Positive finite multiplicities replace the generator by a Morita-equivalent one with the same module category.

**The exact ideal kernel.** The top PBW trace $\tau$ equals $\phi_0\mathrm{reg}$: only the bounded monomial with all exponents $l-1$ and identity permutation reaches the all-column-one fixed-order tensor in top degree. Consequently $\tau(bg)=\lambda(q\,\mathrm{reg}(b))$. If $b\in K$, every $ab\in K$ and $\tau(abg)=0$ for all $a$, so nondegeneracy gives $bg=0$. Hence $H/K\to Hg$, $b+K\mapsto bg$, is well defined and surjective. The exterior row basis has size $(d!/|J|)\prod_j(l-t_j+1)$. In the truncated polynomial/permutation associated graded, with $b_j=t_j-1$, the words $uX^{\mathbf r+\mathbf b}a_-$, $u\in S_d/J$, $0\le r_j\le l-t_j$, are independent: different cosets have disjoint permutation supports and different exponent vectors have different polynomial supports. The bare trace adjoint has RIGHT image $gH$; applying the generator-fixing anti-involution gives the contragredient LEFT image $Hg$.
All roots may repeat, since none was divided by a difference.

Exact parabolic induction supplies $q:T\twoheadrightarrow E(A)$. Natural finite-W transport and regular evaluation identify $\pi(q)$ with the preceding exterior quotient and $\pi(R_g)$ with right multiplication by $g$. A finite total-column-degree filtration makes the nilradical act trivially on its graded finite Levi pieces; complete reducibility refines this to a standard flag of $E(A)$. The projective $T$ also has a standard flag. For any simple submodule $L$ of either standard-filtered object, choose the first flag term meeting $L$ nontrivially; simplicity gives containment there and zero intersection with the preceding term, hence an embedding of $L$ into that standard section. Its label is standard by [F3]. Every nonzero submodule has a simple socle because this is a finite-length chunk, so exactness and the nonzero standard-simple image make $\pi$ detect nonzero SUBMODULES of these two objects. This does not assert conservativity on the whole category. Since $\pi(R_g\ker q)=0$, detection gives $R_g\ker q=0$. Thus $R_g$ factors as $Fq$ with $F:E(A)\to T$. Earlier positions already have columns $t_h\le t_j<i$, while later ones remain in column $l\ge i$, so the native dot formula has no spectator swaps; subtracting $m_i$ leaves exactly the next left shift. It belongs to the actual cumulative-column symmetric submodule $e_SZ(A)$. The map $Hp_+a_+\to e_SZ(A)$ induced by regular evaluation is injective. Its target has dimension $(d!/|J_+|)\prod_j t_j$. Applying $\sigma$ to the displayed ordinary product sends each factor to a unit $-1$ times $(x_j-m_i)$, and the ordinary symmetrizer becomes $a_-$. At a later label the previously identified lower terms constitute the same known family (their multiplicities need not be equal); the new leading term cannot be a member of that family because each leading family is pairwise nonisomorphic. Uniqueness of indecomposable summands therefore identifies the two new leading terms, and cancellation then identifies all lower multiplicities. Let $n\ge0$ be an integer, with $S_0=\{1\}$ as in
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]. Let $A:=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ be the ring of Laurent polynomials in one
indeterminate $v$ over $\mathbb Z$. For $n\ge2$ the **generic type-A Hecke
algebra** $H_v(n)$ is the associative unital $A$-algebra presented by generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ and the relations
$$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v\quad(1\le i<n),\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le n-2),\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(1\le i,j<n,\ |i-j|>1),$$
that is, the quotient of the free unital associative $A$-algebra on
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ by the two-sided ideal generated by these relators. The
first relation is written in the **RG-13 quadratic normalization**
$(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, equivalent to the displayed form over $A$. For $n\le1$ there
are no generators and we set $H_v(n):=A$.

**Standard basis elements.** Let $S_n=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\dots,n\})$ with
simple transpositions $s_i=(i\ i+1)$
([[def-symmetric-group]]), and let $w\in S_n$ have inversion length $\ell(w)=\ell$
([[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]). Choose a reduced expression
$w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}$, that is, a word of the minimal length $\ell(w)$
representing $w$, and put
$$T_w:=T_{i_1}\cdots T_{i_\ell}\in H_v(n),$$
the empty product when $w$ is the identity of $S_n$, so that $T_w=1$ for that
element. That $T_w$ is independent of the chosen reduced expression, and that
the elements $T_w$ form an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$, is proved in the
standard-basis theorem below
([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]); the notation
distinguishes the generator $T_i$ with $1\le i\le n-1$ from $T_w$ for the group
element $w$.

**Specializations.** Let $R$ be a commutative $A$-algebra with structure map
$\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to R$, $v\mapsto v_0$, and suppose $v_0\in R^\times$. The
**specialization** of $H_v(n)$ at $v_0$ is the $R$-algebra
$R\otimes_AH_v(n)$; it is presented over $R$ by the images of $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$
subject to the same relations with $v$ replaced by $v_0$, and we write $H_{v_0}(n)$
for it. Two specializations are used on this page: $v\mapsto1$, where the
quadratic relation becomes $T_i^2=1$ together with the braid and commutation
relations, and $v\mapsto q$, where $q$ is the prime power defining
$\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$; the latter specializes the generic algebra to
the Hecke algebra attached to the finite general linear group. The condition
$v_0\in R^\times$ is part of the definition of a specialization and, for a nonzero coefficient ring $R$, excludes $v_0=0$. The zero ring
is allowed: its unique element is a unit and its specialization is the zero algebra.

Work over the field $\mathbb C$ and fix an integer $d\ge 0$
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], [[def-commutative-ring]]). Let
$\mathcal F_d$ be the free associative unital $\mathbb C$-algebra on the
$d+\max(d-1,0)$ symbols $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ (for $d=0$ there is only
the unit; for $d=1$ only $x_1$), with its word basis and universal property
([[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]]), and let
$I_d\mathrel{\trianglelefteq}\mathcal F_d$ be the two-sided ideal
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]])
generated by the following elements:

- $x_ix_j-x_jx_i$ for all $1\le i,j\le d$;
- $s_i^2-1$, $s_is_{i+1}s_i-s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1}$, and $s_is_j-s_js_i$ for
  $|i-j|>1$, for $1\le i,j\le d-1$;
- $s_ix_j-x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$, $s_ix_{i+1}-x_is_i-1$, and
  $x_{i+1}s_i-s_ix_i-1$, for $1\le i\le d-1$ and $1\le j\le d$.

The **degenerate affine Hecke algebra** is the quotient $\mathbb C$-algebra
$$H_d:=\mathcal F_d/I_d$$
with unit element written $1$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]). We keep the symbols
$x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ for their images, and for $w\in S_d$ we write
$w$ for the image in $H_d$ of any word in the $s_i$ representing $w$; this is
independent of the chosen word once the basis theorem below is proved. For
$d\ge1$ and $a\in\mathbb C$, the notation $H_d/(x_1-a)$ means the quotient by the two-sided
ideal generated by $x_1-a$.

The verification below establishes exactly the structure of $H_d$ used
throughout this page: the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad r_1,\dots,r_d\ge0,\ w\in S_d,$$
form a $\mathbb C$-basis, so that
$H_d\cong\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[S_d]$ as a vector
space with polynomial and group-algebra subalgebras
([[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]], [[def-group-ring]]);
$H_0=\mathbb C$ and $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$; for $d\ge1$ and every $a$ there is a unique
algebra isomorphism
$$H_d/(x_1-a)\cong\mathbb C[S_d],\qquad x_j\longmapsto a+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j);$$
and total polynomial degree is an algebra filtration whose associated graded is
the semidirect product $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$ in which
$s_i$ acts by swapping $x_i$ and $x_{i+1}$. For $d\ge2$, the cross relation is
inhomogeneous, so it does not turn $H_d$ into a graded algebra with
$\deg x_i=1$ and $\deg s_i=0$. For $d=0$ the algebra $\mathbb C$ has its
degree-zero grading, and for $d=1$ the algebra $\mathbb C[x_1]$ has its
natural polynomial grading.

Let $H_d$ be the degenerate affine Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] and let
$\mathbf a=(a_1,\dots,a_l)$ be a multiset of complex numbers, $l\ge1$. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is $H_0(\mathbf a)=\mathbb C$ for $d=0$, and for $d\ge1$ is the quotient
$$H_d(\mathbf a):=H_d\Big/\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-a_j)\Bigr),$$
the two-sided ideal being the one generated by the displayed polynomial
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]],
[[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the tensor-realization verification below; the quotient definition itself is choice-free.

The verification below records the structure of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ used on this
page. A $\mathbb C$-basis is given by the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad 0\le r_1,\dots,r_d<l,\ w\in S_d,$$
so that $\dim H_d(\mathbf a)=l^dd!$; the polynomial-degree filtration has
associated graded the algebra
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. For
integral roots $a_j\in\mathbb Z$ this is the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$
attached to the dominant weight $\Lambda=\sum_j m_j\Lambda_j$ of the integer
type-A root system, with $m_j=\#\{i:a_i=j\}$; for general complex roots one
uses a separate integer chain in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$, and the
symbol $\Lambda_a$ denotes a formal fundamental weight on that chain, not an
index of the integer-only lattice. The pyramid roots of the finite-W-algebra
constructions are $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the
pyramid columns $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. If $l=1$, then
$x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ in the quotient. The generator-fixing
anti-involution of $H_d$ descends to $H_d(\mathbf a)$. The top coefficient
functional of the monomial basis is a nondegenerate symmetric trace on
$H_d(\mathbf a)$, and it restricts to a nondegenerate trace on every central
block corner.

Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $z\in A$ be a unit. Fix an integer
$n\ge0$.

**The nondegenerate affine presentation.** The algebra
$H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}(A;z)$ is the $A$-algebra presented by commuting units
$X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]],
[[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]) subject to
$$T_r^2=(z-1)T_r+z,\qquad T_rT_{r+1}T_r=T_{r+1}T_rT_{r+1},\qquad T_rT_s=T_sT_r\quad(|r-s|>1),$$
$$T_rX_rT_r=zX_{r+1},\qquad T_rX_s=X_sT_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
the last two relations being the Bernstein relation and the distant mixed
commutation, and with $T_r$ invertible as a consequence of its quadratic
relation. For $n=0$ the algebra is $A$.

**The degenerate affine presentation.** The algebra
$H_n^{\deg}(A)$ is the $A$-algebra presented by commuting generators
$x_1,\dots,x_n$ and symmetric-group generators $s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}$ subject to
the Coxeter relations $s_r^2=1$, $s_rs_{r+1}s_r=s_{r+1}s_rs_{r+1}$,
$s_rs_t=s_ts_r$ for $|r-t|>1$ together with the mixed relations
$$s_rx_r=x_{r+1}s_r-1,\qquad s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1,\qquad s_rx_t=x_ts_r\quad(t\notin\{r,r+1\}).$$

**Auxiliary cyclotomic quotients.** For a monic polynomial
$f(u)=u^{\ell}+a_{\ell-1}u^{\ell-1}+\dots+a_0$ in $A[u]$ of degree $\ell$
impose the single relation $f(X_1)=0$ (respectively $f(x_1)=0$) on the FIRST
polynomial generator and call the resulting quotient the **monic cyclotomic
quotient**; when $\ell=0$, so that $f=1$, the quotient at positive rank is the
zero algebra, while rank zero remains $A$. In the nondegenerate case the
constant term $a_0$ is required to be a unit. The first-strand convention
imposed here (cyclotomic relation on $X_1$, and later induction appending on
the right) is the one used on this page.

**The charged cyclic specialization.** Let $A=F$ be a field, let
$z=q_H\in F^{\times}$ have finite quantum characteristic $e\ge2$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), and let
$I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ be the cyclic **label set** of residues, with a
dominant cyclic type-A weight $(\lambda_i)_{i\in I}$, $\lambda_i\ge0$, and
$\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). If $q_H\ne1$ use the
nondegenerate presentation and put $c_i:=q_H^{\,i}$; if $q_H=1$ (which forces
$\operatorname{char}F=e$) use the degenerate presentation and put
$c_i:=i\cdot1_F$. Impose
$$f(z_1)=\prod_{i\in I}(z_1-c_i)^{\lambda_i}$$
on the first generator ($z_1=X_1$ in the nondegenerate branch and $z_1=x_1$ in
the degenerate branch) and write $H_d^\Lambda$ for the resulting **charged
cyclotomic quotient** of rank $d$. This charged finite-$e$ branch is the scope
of the present page; the arbitrary-base affine and monic definitions above
supply its universal PBW and trace proof inputs. The definition itself asserts
no basis, no spectrum, no primitive block decomposition and no
Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism. The grading variable $v$ of the KLR side is
independent of $q_H$.

**Well-definedness notes.** The nondegenerate parameters $c_i=q_H^i$ are
distinct because $q_H$ has multiplicative order exactly $e$; the degenerate
parameters $c_i=i\cdot1_F$ are distinct because $\operatorname{char}F=e$ makes
$i\cdot1_F\ne j\cdot1_F$ for $0\le i<j<e$. In the nondegenerate branch no
embedding of the label set $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ into $F$ is claimed or used:
$i$ is only a label for the value $q_H^i$. All these definitions are given by
generators, relations and a two-sided quotient ideal and use no choice
principle.

derivations.claim: In the degenerate quotient $x_1=m$ and $sx_2=ms+1$ give $x_2=m+s$. Hence the quotient is generated by $s$ with $s^2=1$. Conversely the assignments $x_1\mapsto m$, $x_2\mapsto m+s$, $s\mapsto s$ in $\mathbb C[s]/(s^2-1)$ satisfy both cross relations and commutativity, so they define an inverse to the map sending $s$ into the quotient. Evaluation at $s=1,-1$ identifies this algebra with $\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, with inverse $(a,b)\mapsto(a+b)/2+(a-b)s/2$. In particular it has no nonzero nilpotents and has precisely the two one-dimensional simple modules $s=1,-1$.

At $\xi=-1$, step 1.2 and [F1] give $H_{-1}(2)=\mathbb C[T]/((T+1)^2)$. Setting $\varepsilon=T+1$ identifies it with $B=\mathbb C[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$, whose basis is $1,\varepsilon$ by division by the monic polynomial $\varepsilon^2$. Thus $\varepsilon$ is nonzero and nilpotent. Every $a+b\varepsilon$ with $a\ne0$ has inverse $a^{-1}-ba^{-2}\varepsilon$; those with $a=0$ are nonunits. Consequently $(\varepsilon)$ is the unique maximal ideal and is the nonzero radical. Every simple $B$-module is killed by $\varepsilon$: its image under this central operator is a submodule, and if the image were the whole nonzero simple module, its square could not vanish. The unique simple is therefore $B/(\varepsilon)\cong\mathbb C$.

The two algebras cannot be isomorphic: an isomorphism would send the nonzero square-zero element of step 2.1 to a nonzero nilpotent in the algebra of step 1.1. Their decomposition behavior also differs directly. The regular module of $\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$ is the direct sum of its two simples. The regular module $B$ has the filtration $0\subset(\varepsilon)\subset B$ with both subquotients equal to its unique simple; it is indecomposable since an idempotent $a+b\varepsilon$ satisfies $a^2=a$ and $2ab=b$, forcing it to be $0$ or $1$. Steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1 disprove the claimed universal algebra transport and step 2.2 exhibits its failure in a concrete comparison formula. The witness uses the entire rank-two algebras, with the degenerate full integer residue set; it is not a comparison with a supported cut retaining only the charge $m$. For a finite degenerate cut containing this entire example the root interval must contain $m-1,m,m+1$, since $x_2=m\pm1$ on its two simples. In the nondegenerate level-one quotient [F3], $X_1=Q$ and $X_2=Q\xi^{-1}T^2$, so it is generated by $T$. Conversely in the finite algebra $H_\xi(2)$ of [F1], $T^{-1}=\xi^{-1}(T-(\xi-1))$. At rank two the limitation can be seen in an actual comparison formula. For $\xi\ne-1$ put $a=(\xi-1)/2$ and $b=(\xi+1)/2$. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited through the Skryabin, natural
Whittaker and category-O projective/tilting suppliers. The finite Hecke
calculations below require only finite-dimensional linear algebra.

For $I=\mathbb Z$ (and reflected auxiliary finite cuts used to realize this
global statement), the map $t$ sends $\Lambda_i$ to $\Lambda_{-i}$ and
$\alpha_i$ to $\alpha_{-i}$, so $m^t=(-m_l,\dots,-m_1)$. The sign map
$\sigma(s_r)=-s_r$, $\sigma(x_r)=-x_r$ gives
$H^\Lambda_\alpha\cong H^{\Lambda^t}_{\alpha^t}$ and intertwines residue $i$
with $-i$. Multipartition transpose with reversed components gives
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha\cong\mathrm{Col}^{\Lambda^t}_{\alpha^t}$, sending
$\mathrm{Rev}$ to target $\mathrm{Std}$. The genuine sourced Specht/sign
comparison is $\sigma^*S(A^t)\cong S(A)^{\circledast}$, and for
$A\in\mathrm{Rev}$ the simple and projective-cover labels are $A^t\mapsto A^\downarrow$;
no off-standard $D(A)$ is made into a simple. At parameter one these are maps on
the projected highest constituent/costandard and standard lattices, rather than
a naive permutation of all simple labels or all ambient monomial vectors.

For a finite bounded category-O chunk define $Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A)=\pi P_{\mathcal O}(A)$
for EVERY $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, and
$\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A)=\pi T_{\mathcal O}(A)$ for EVERY
$A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$. The existing signed-Young comparison identifies
$\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A)$ with $\sigma^*Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A^t)$; on

Schur-cover algebra, and

Ringel dual. Off-standard $Y_{\mathrm{all}}$ are indecomposable nonprojective

using $F=D\Psi$ with its explicit shifts and
