derivations.claim: **The eight ambient labels.** There is one bipartition of size zero, two of size one and five of size two: $(\varnothing,\varnothing)$; $(\varnothing,1),(1,\varnothing)$; and $(1,1),(\varnothing,2),(2,\varnothing),(\varnothing,11),(11,\varnothing)$. The ground-difference column rule at charge $(0,0)$ gives respectively $OO,OU,UO,UU,OR,RO,OC,CO$, so $C0$ has the vertical partition in the first component and $0C$ in the second. Subtracting the ground weights gives degree $0$ for $00$, $\alpha_0$ for $01,10$, $2\alpha_0$ for $11$, $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ for $0R,R0$, and $\alpha_0+\alpha_{-1}$ for $0C,C0$. Strict columns with weakly increasing rows select $00,01,11,0R,0C$; reverse-standard rows select $00,10,11,R0,C0$. Reading the two columns and inserting in this small window gives $10^\downarrow=01$, $R0^\downarrow=0R$, $C0^\downarrow=0C$ and fixes $00,11$. Component reversal and partition transpose give precisely the displayed ambient permutation.

**The full height-two window.** With $x=x_1$, $y=x_2$, $u=s_1$ the relations give $u^2=1$, $[x,y]=0$, $ux=yu-1$, $uy=xu+1$ and $x^2=0$; from $ux^2=0$ one derives $y^2=(x+y)u$, and reducing by this relation decreases the $y$-exponent while killing $x$-exponents at least two, so the eight words $1,x,y,xy,u,xu,yu,xyu$ span the degree-two algebra. The three models $(N,-N,-J)$ on $M_2(\mathbb C)$ with $N=E_{12}$ and $J$ the swap matrix, $(\epsilon,1+\epsilon,1)$ on $B_+$, and $(\epsilon,-1+\epsilon,-1)$ on $B_-$ satisfy the relations by direct matrix computation; the central element $z=x+y$ has images $0$, $1+2\epsilon$ and $-1+2\epsilon$, and the Hermite polynomials $E_0=(1-z^2)^2$, $E_\pm=(1-E_0\pm(3z-z^3)/2)/2$ map to the three separate identities. Each factor is generated by its images of $x$ and $u$, so the map is surjective onto the eight-dimensional product and the spanning bound makes it an isomorphism; hence there are no other height-two blocks and $H_0,H_1$ are the direct factors listed. The two-dimensional simple of $M_2(\mathbb C)$ carries the generator-fixed contravariant form $J$, since $N^{t}J=JN$ and $(-J)^{t}J=J(-J)$; sign is inner on $M_2(\mathbb C)$ via conjugation by $K=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ (which satisfies $KN=-NK$ and $KJ=-JK$), so the unique simple and its cover are fixed there, while on $B_\pm$ sign identifies $\epsilon$ with $-\epsilon$ and exchanges the two factors, fixing the unique objects of those contents as classes.

**The projected vectors and the transpose.** Normalizing the highest pairing $C_0$ makes the two-term highest sums have norm two, so the dual projected vectors are the half-sums $D_{01}=\tfrac12(M_{01}+M_{10})$, $D_{0R}=\tfrac12(M_{0R}+M_{R0})$, $D_{0C}=\tfrac12(M_{0C}+M_{C0})$, and the projective cover vectors are the unhalved sums with endpoints $P_{00}=D_{00}$, $P_{11}=D_{11}$. Applying the mixed residue operators $f_1$ and $f_{-1}$ to the mixed highest vector gives $T_{R0}=M_{R0}+s^{-1}M_{0R}$ and $T_{C0}=M_{C0}+s^{-1}M_{0C}$, with kernels $L_{R0}=M_{R0}-sM_{0R}$ and $L_{C0}=M_{C0}-sM_{0C}$, so at parameter one these kernel vectors have zero projected image and the projected vectors are the displayed half-sums. The ambient monomial transpose at parameter one fixes the ground, commutes with the reflected Chevalley operators (transposing each column negates its contents and the coproduct is cocommutative), and therefore descends to the highest constituent, where it fixes $P_{01}/D_{01}$ and exchanges $P_{0R}/D_{0R}$ with $P_{0C}/D_{0C}$; it does not swap $P_{01}$ with the ambient $P_{10}$, and the off-standard vectors $D_{10},D_{R0},D_{C0}$ are zero by [F2]. This is the projected-lattice clause of [F1] on the eight-label window.

**The intrinsic Young and signed images.** Verify the tables from the intrinsic ideals rather than assuming a projective-preservation theorem. In $B_0=\mathbb C[x]/x^2$ the reduced permutation ideal of the label $01$ is $B_0$, and of the reverse label $10$ it is $(x)$; in $B_\pm$ the reduced permutation ideals are $B_\pm$ or $(xy)=(\pm\epsilon)$, where the row factor $1\pm u$ equals $2$ when it occurs; in $M_2(\mathbb C)$ both labels $11$ give the left ideal $M_2N$, the unique simple cover. Every such ideal is indecomposable in its explicit block, so the intrinsic Young definition identifies them exactly: $Y_{00}=\mathbb C$, $Y_{01}=B_0$, $Y_{10}=D_{01}$, $Y_{11}=D_{11}$, $Y_{0R}=B_+$, $Y_{R0}=D_{0R}$, $Y_{0C}=B_-$, $Y_{C0}=D_{0C}$, with cover labels exactly $\mathrm{Std}$. The signed reduced permutation ideals of the same labels give $\widetilde Y_{00}=\mathbb C$, $\widetilde Y_{01}=D_{01}$, $\widetilde Y_{10}=B_0$, $\widetilde Y_{11}=D_{11}$, $\widetilde Y_{0R}=D_{0R}$, $\widetilde Y_{R0}=B_+$, $\widetilde Y_{0C}=D_{0C}$, $\widetilde Y_{C0}=B_-$, with cover labels exactly $\mathrm{Rev}$; no higher summand or nonexistent off-standard simple is needed.

**The sign formula on $\mathrm{Rev}$.** For $A=10,R0,C0$, respectively, $A^t=01,0C,0R$ and $A^\downarrow=01,0R,0C$. By the tables of step 3.2, $Y(A^t)=B_0,B_-,B_+$; the sign action of step 2.1 sends these to $B_0,B_+,B_-$, respectively. These are both $\widetilde Y(A)$ and $Y(A^\downarrow)$. For $A=00,11$ all three classes agree and are fixed by sign. Thus $\widetilde Y(A)=\sigma^*Y(A^t)\cong Y(A^\downarrow)$ holds for every reverse-standard label in the window. Each displayed Specht is self-dual under the generator-fixed duality in its block: it is one dimensional in $B_0,B_\pm$, while the matrix-block simple has the explicit form $J$ of step 2.1. The transpose exchanges the two adjacent contents, and their one-dimensional generator actions are carried into each other by sign, proving the Specht formula here as well.

**Conclusion.** Step 1.1 verifies the full eight-label ambient window and the rectification; step 2.1 proves the complete height-two algebra, hence the exact block models and the sign action; step 3.1 verifies the projected simple and cover vectors and the effect of the ambient transpose on the highest constituent, including its failure to swap $P_{01}$ with $P_{10}$; steps 3.2 and 4.1 verify the full Young and signed tables from the intrinsic ideals and the formula $\widetilde Y(A)=\sigma^*Y(A^t)\cong Y(A^\downarrow)$ on $\mathrm{Rev}$.
